subject: Private VPC: runbook & failover roster for SLA exception
messages:
From: Samantha Ross <samantha.ross@helixsystems.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: ops@helixsystems.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC: request for runbook + failover roster for SLA exception

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Helix is running Redwood’s private deployment behind our own regional edge that we manage. We’re seeing intermittent 200–400 ms token-latency spikes on large-batch inference during our afternoon peak window; our infra team suspects a NAT translation burst on the edge routers that coincides with daily backups.

Per our contract appendix, Helix is responsible for customer-controlled infra, but we need a formal SLA exception that documents the operational boundary and the explicit failover/runbook that Redwood will execute when client-side routing causes sustained latency above the agreed SLOs. This needs to include:
- An agreed escalation path (who Redwood will call inside Helix)
- A 24/7 on-call roster for Redwood for the initial 30-day remediation window
- A short runbook with triggers (latency thresholds, metrics) and automated fallback behavior (model variant + reduced batch size)

Can you confirm Redwood can sign off on a short exception letter and share the runbook + contacts this week? We’d like to align before our next scheduled maintenance on Sep 25.

Attached: sample latency graph (PNG stub), network-capture-summary.txt (referenced)

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Ross
Head of Platform Ops, Helix Systems
+samantha.ross@helixsystems.com
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Samantha Ross <samantha.ross@helixsystems.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: request for runbook + failover roster for SLA exception

Samantha — thanks for the summary and the graph. We’re happy to put an operational exception letter in place that codifies the split-responsibility and our fast-fail behaviors. High level plan below; I’ll loop in Karthik (customer lead) and Neha (legal/compliance) for signoff on the wording.

Planned deliverables (target: EOD Mon 2027-09-20):
1) Draft exception letter that specifies which latency buckets are attributed to Helix-managed edge vs Redwood (and how evidence will be collected)
2) A concise runbook (PDF) with:
   - Triggers: 95th percentile token latency > 250 ms sustained for 5 minutes OR error rate > 0.5%
   - Immediate action: switch to a lower-batch, quantized model variant in the same region + enable prefix cache bypass mode
   - If still > threshold after 10 minutes: route traffic to Redwood Dedicated pool in next-closest region (documented fallback)
3) A 30-day on-call roster proposal (week-by-week, with escalation numbers)

Questions for Helix:
- Who will be the escalation contacts we call for initial network checks? (Name + mobile + PST business hours)
- Can Helix provide packet captures around the next maintenance window so we can reproduce the burst pattern in our staging environment?

I’ve attached a first-pass posture document and an internal runbook stub for engineering. Karthik — please advise if we should offer a limited SLA credit during the 30-day remediation window or propose a technical mitigation plan only. Neha — please advise legal language to cover evidence collection and audit windows.

Best,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, Samantha Ross <samantha.ross@helixsystems.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: request for runbook + failover roster for SLA exception

Team — quick operational alignment. I reviewed Mateo’s runbook stub and proposed triggers. From a commercial standpoint, Helix is a mid-size strategic account (HLX-4721) and we should scope a 30-day remediation window where Redwood provides the runbook and executes the documented fallbacks without immediate credits, but we’ll offer a one-time service credit if the fallback path fails to restore SLOs within the 30-day window.

Priyom — can you confirm we can staff the on-call roster (two engineers rotating, primary + backup) for the 30-day period starting Sep 21? Also confirm the Dedicated-pool warm-up time and any capacity reservation needed to guarantee route-to-Dedicated within 10 minutes.

Neha — please propose exception language that preserves Helix audit rights (logs, packet captures) while protecting Redwood from unbounded liability for customer-managed edge issues. I suggest limiting the exception to performance attribution only (no change to uptime SLA).

Samantha — will this commercial approach work from Helix’s side? If yes, Mateo & I will circulate the draft letter and runbook for signatures.

—Karthik
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, Samantha Ross <samantha.ross@helixsystems.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: request for runbook + failover roster for SLA exception

Karthik / Mateo — confirmed. We can staff the on-call rotation starting Sep 21: two primary engineers (PST days), one backup (overnights). Warm-up for Dedicated pool: 7 minutes for instance handshake and KV cache population for the smaller quantized variant; full KV warm-up for large-context models can be up to 18 minutes. We’ll document the warm-up guarantees and include a playbook step that proactively pre-warms a standby shard if Helix notifies us 30 min before scheduled maintenance.

Action items completed:
- Attaching the runbook (vpc-fallback-runbook-v1.pdf) and the proposed on-call roster (helix-failover-roster.xlsx).
- Draft exception letter (linked): https://redwood.app/drive/HLX-4721/runbooks/vpc-fallback

Samantha — please confirm escalation contacts and whether Helix will provide targeted captures during the Sep 25 maintenance so we can validate the mitigation. Once Helix confirms, Neha and I will finalize the exception letter for signature.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
(attachment stubs: vpc-fallback-runbook-v1.pdf (pdf), helix-failover-roster.xlsx (xlsx))
